messages:
lee: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a 'quality-continuity adaptor' to smooth transitions when we switch quant profiles mid-request. Idea: track recent token-level degradation and apply lightweight reconstruction or temporarily up-precision for the next N tokens.

maya: Sounds useful. Is this a per-endpoint flag or a runtime subsystem?

lee: Runtime component attached to PrecisionProfile. Minimal API change: add a small continuity block to the profile so product teams can opt in per-endpoint.

lee: Example sketch of the profile snippet:

```
continuity: {
  window_tokens: 32,            # lookback window for quality signal
  deg_threshold: 0.12,         # degradation score threshold to trigger
  hysteresis_tokens: 8,        # keep behavior for this many tokens after trigger
  repair_model: "tiny-recon-v1"  # optional postprocess model name
}
```

ravi: How do we compute deg_threshold in practice? degscore? KL on softmax? topk-shift? Need something robust and cheap.

sophia: I'd prefer a composite: degscore (model-calibrated) + topk-shift heuristic. Use exponentially-weighted decay so one spike doesn't flip the world.

pat: Ops note: repair_model implies additional model loads. If customers enable this, we need separate pools or a soft quota to avoid contention.

lee: Agreed — default repair_model = none. Two runtime options when continuity trips: (A) force a temporary higher-precision lane for the hysteresis window, or (B) generate normally and postprocess via repair_model. Both have tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs output fidelity).

maya: Forcing higher precision reduces degradation quickly but could blow cost/latency. We should gate it with a budget and per-minute limits.

lee: Proposal: profile fields `continuity_budget_per_minute` and `continuity_max_concurrency` so ops can cap behavior. Also expose telemetry: continuity.triggers, average latency delta, cost delta, and reduction in degscore.

ops-bot: Deploy reminder: if repair_model is used, put it on a separate worker pool tagged `continuity-repair` and set low burst concurrency.

ravi: Also need a canary rollout knob: continuity.canary_percent so we can phase-in on a subset of traffic and compare with shadow baseline.

sophia: Important: when switching precision mid-request, stash and restore KV-cache prefix so we don't corrupt attention state. Add an atomic handoff in the runtime.

lee: Good catch. Runtime sketch will include `kv_checkpoint` + `reconcile_on_restore` flags.

maya: For evals: run shadow traffic with repair_model enabled + metric: %tokens improved (degscore drop), p95 latency, token cost delta. If >X% improvement at <Y% cost, we enable for canary.

lee: I'll draft a PR with schema, a runtime impl sketch, and an eval plan. Will include sample JSON schemas, telemetry fields, and an ops runbook (how to rollback continuity canary).

maya: Thanks — ping me for QA and the eval harness.

lee: Will do. Filing follow-up doc in RFC tracker — will link in PR.
